signals.evidence: Air raid sirens activated in Upper Galilee border towns near Lebanon with immediate shelter-in-place directives issued in preparation for potential rocket attack
Firefighters handled suspicious package at airport with precautionary evacuation; military intercepted rocket launched from Iran toward northern territory
Strong explosions heard in Haifa Bay area; Iranian Revolutionary Guards confirmed five casualties from Israeli-American strike on Ardabil province
Senior Sergeant Gai Ludari killed by friendly fire during Hezbollah terrorist detention operation in village of Shiba in Lebanon
Police clashes with anti-war demonstrators near Habima Theatre in Tel Aviv; at least 17 demonstrators detained; one injured and lost consciousness when air raid alarm sounded
Israeli Supreme Court ruled to expand permitted demonstration participation from 150 to 600 people near Habima Theatre, overriding military command restrictions
Schools preparing gradual return after Passover; teaching expected to resume April 12 in reduced format; Ben-Gurion Airport flight restrictions being eased beginning that day

Home Front Command Colonel Aviberma: 'Passover camps are open and permitted. Special education for children with special needs is also allowed' with requirement that 'all 30 children into a safe room' within 60 seconds of alarm

Home Front Command Colonel: emergency directives remain unchanged; Passover camps approved by command are operating with proximity to bomb shelters and air raid protocols requiring shelter entry within one minute
Home Front Command Colonel: 'Some municipalities have not accepted this, some have complied' regarding restrictions on special needs school activities near bomb shelters during air raid alerts
Home Front Command official: '80% of injuries during this war occurred at home as a result of careless actions heading to shelters'

Home Front Command official emphasizes careful, methodical responses to alerts: stopping vehicles safely on roadsides, using emergency signals, entering shelters cautiously to prevent injuries during evacuation
Home Front Command Colonel: 'Home Front Command tries to allow routine life to continue on one hand while preserving life on the other' and 'If instructions are changed, we will announce it'

Home Front Command Colonel acknowledges tension: High Court authorized 600 people at Tel Aviv demonstration while military command restricts other gatherings to 150 people; 'We all bow to court decisions even if we don't like them'

Home Front Command official advises civilians to use Home Front Command mobile application with location services enabled to receive threat alerts during outdoor activities when sirens cannot be heard

Northern Israel education director: 'Much less damage in the north today' and 'The citizens are standing at the front, they are the spearhead, they mark the way for us, and we must appreciate the people of the north very much'
Northern Israel education director: civilians have adapted to brief 15-second warning periods; much incoming fire is directed at Israeli military forces within Lebanon rather than civilian targets

Official addresses immigrant population: 'Every one of us is doing something for the success of the war' and urges parents to 'take care of them, engage them, create connection with them... the most important thing is to take care of children—this is part of the war effort'
Israeli Supreme Court Chief Justice Yitzhak Amit: 'if we prohibit demonstrations, then this will no longer be a democratic state'
Football matches resuming without spectators during wartime, indicating partial return to routine activities
Senior sergeant killed in friendly fire during counter-terrorism operation in southern Lebanon; Iran launched missile attacks on Israel and Kuwait; air defenses intercepted weapons
Schools preparing for partial return to school right after Passover holiday; learning may gradually resume April 12 in shortened format pending security clearance
Education correspondent: 'Everything is very differential; some cities have no shelter at all, some authorities have nowhere even to hold studies'
Education correspondent: phased classroom resumption prioritizes early grades contingent on Home Front Command security approval; 'some cities have no shelter at all'
Education correspondent: 'For younger age groups this will be somewhat more complicated because most facilities are less protected or lack shelter entirely'

Education correspondent confirms traffic-light threat system remains in effect with continuous color changes; 'We are also managing services or transportation; suddenly there are more transports, suddenly there are fewer'
Education official: 'Many educational institutions are still serving as shelters. Not every neighborhood has a shelter—some have none at all'
Education official: 'There are no clear answers. We don't know what happens with transportation—we saw just a month ago that schools were hit by rockets'
Education correspondent: 'The intention is to return preschoolers, first, second, and possibly third graders, and exam-year students after Passover. But in what form, how—that's still unclear'
Education correspondent: 'Each municipality will ultimately make decisions based on their own reasoning. Some oppose such arrangements, and there's no unified decision'

Education official: 'No one clearly understands who will take responsibility. There's no way to safely operate the shuttles' and 'The situation where children must shelter during an alert while on a shuttle—that's also very complicated'
Ben-Gurion Airport: passenger load raised from 50 to 80 persons per outbound flight; only one outbound and one inbound flight per hour permitted
During Passover week, normally 1.5 million Israelis travel; current operations at very low, very limited numbers
Of 80 available seats: 20 designated for humanitarian cases via Transport Ministry urgent committee; 60 allocated by ticket purchase date
Israeli airlines operating at drastically reduced capacity with near-empty flights generating minimal revenue; foreign airlines barred from operating to Israel until mid-month

Air raid alarm on northern front: 'заходите в изолированные комнаты или в убежище, где вам, я напоминаю, следует находиться не менее 10 минут после' (enter isolated rooms or shelters, remain at least 10 minutes after all-clear)

Caller reports Telegram account compromised; fraudulent messages sent to contacts asking for money: 'от вашего имени вашим друзьям придет сообщение, что вы, не дай бог, в тяжелом материальном положении'
Second caller reports similar Telegram compromise affecting alternate account; fraudulent messages sent from alternate phone number as well
Caller received suspicious call from person claiming to be from radio station OREC asking about Russian-language speakers at bank; caller did not initiate inquiry
Caller reports: 'I was scared because of this' upon receiving suspicious call claiming to be from radio station
Caller warns listeners: 'When someone calls you and you hear it is a scammer, understand it immediately, hang up from the left side, do not talk to suspicious phones'
Senior Sergeant Gai Ludar, 21 years old, killed in South Lebanon during counterterrorism operation; died from friendly fire due to identification error
